'''Giovanni Felder''' (18 November 1958 in [[Aarau]]) is a Swiss mathematical physicist and mathematician, working at ETH Zurich. He specializes in algebraic and geometric properties of [[integrable]] models of [[statistical mechanics]] and [[quantum field theory]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Felder, Giovanni, Prof. Dr.|website=ETH Zürich, Mathematics Department|url=https://www.math.ethz.ch/research/mathematical-physics/giovanni-felder.html}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Felder attended school in [[Lugano]] and [[Willisau District]]. He studied physics at [[ETH Zurich]], where he graduated with M.Sc. in 1982 and with Ph.D. in 1986.<ref name=ias>{{cite web|title=Giovanni Felder|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/giovanni-felder}}</ref> His doctoral dissertation, entitled ''Renormalization Group, Tree Expansion, and Non-renormalizable Quantum Field Theories'', was supervised by [[Jürg Fröhlich]] (and [[Konrad Osterwalder]]).<ref name=":0">{{MathGenealogy|id=54311}}</ref>

Felder held postdoctoral positions from 1986 to 1988 at [[IHES]], from 1988 to 1989 at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]],<ref name="ias" /> and from 1989 to 1991 at the Institute of Theoretical Physics, ETH Zurich.

From 1991 to 1994 he became an assistant professor of mathematics at ETH Zurich. From 1994 to 1996 he worked as professor of mathematics at the [[University of North Carolina]]. In 1996 he returned at ETH Zurich as professor of mathematics.<ref name="AE">{{cite web|title=Giovanni Felder|website=Academia Europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Felder_Giovanni}}</ref> From 2013 to 2019, he was the director of the Institute for Theoretical Studies at ETH Zurich.<ref>{{cite web|date=15 May 2013|title=50 million Swiss francs to Institute for Theoretical Studies|website=EurekAlert!, American Association for the Advancement of Science|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/771780}}</ref>

In 1994 Felder was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers#1994, Zürich|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Zurich.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.2/ICM1994.2.ocr.pdf |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematician |year=1994 |editor-last=Chatterji |editor-first=Srishti Dhar |location=Basel |pages=1247}}</ref> He was elected member of the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2012<ref name="AE" /> and fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Felder's research involves mathematical problems motivated by physical ideas.

In the late 1980s Felder did research with [[Krzysztof Gawedzki]] and [[Antti Kupiainen]] on the geometry of the [[Wess-Zumino-Witten model]] in [[conformal field theory]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Felder |first1=G. |last2=Gawędzki |first2=K. |author-link2=Krzysztof Gawedzki |last3=Kupiainen |first3=A. |author-link3=Antti Kupiainen |year=1988 |title=Spectra of Wess-Zumino-Witten models with arbitrary simple groups |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=117 |issue=1 |pages=127–158 |bibcode=1988CMaPh.117..127F |doi=10.1007/BF01228414 |s2cid=119767773|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1104161597 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Felder |first1=G. |last2=Gawȩdzki |first2=K. |author-link2=Krzysztof Gawedzki |last3=Kupiainen |first3=A. |author-link3=Antti Kupiainen |year=1988 |title=The spectrum of Wess-Zumino-Witten models |journal=Nuclear Physics B |volume=299 |issue=2 |pages=355–366 |bibcode=1988NuPhB.299..355F |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(88)90288-X}}</ref> In 1989 he introduced a [[BRST quantization|BRST]] approach to the "minimal two-dimensional conformal invariant models of [[Alexander Belavin|Belavin]], [[Alexander Markovich Polyakov|Polyakov]] and [[Alexander Zamolodchikov|Zamolodchikov]]."<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(89)90568-3|title=BRST approach to minimal models|year=1989|last1=Felder|first1=Giovanni|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=317|issue=1|pages=215–236|bibcode=1989NuPhB.317..215F}}</ref>

With [[Alexander Varchenko]] and Vitaly Tarasov, Felder did research on various [[integrable]] models<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Felder |first1=Giovanni |last2=Varchenko |first2=Alexander |author-link2=Alexander Varchenko |last3=Tarasov |first3=Vitaly |year=1996 |title=Solutions of the elliptic qKZB equations and Bethe ansatz I |arxiv=q-alg/9606005 }}</ref> in [[quantum field theory]] and [[statistical mechanics]] and resulting [[special functions]] (such as the [[elliptic gamma function]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Felder |first1=Giovanni |last2=Varchenko |first2=Alexander |author-link2=Alexander Varchenko |year=2000 |title=The Elliptic Gamma Function and SL(3, Z)⋉Z<sup>3</sup>{{spaces|2}} |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=156 |pages=44–76 |arxiv=math/9907061 |doi=10.1006/aima.2000.1951 |doi-access=free |s2cid=16762932}}</ref> elliptic [[quantum group]]s,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Felder |first1=Giovanni |last2=Varchenko |first2=Alexander |author-link2=Alexander Varchenko |year=1996 |title=On representations of the elliptic quantum group <math>E</math><sub>τ,η</sub><math>(sl_2)</math> |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=181 |issue=3 |pages=741–761 |arxiv=q-alg/9601003 |bibcode=1996CMaPh.181..741F |doi=10.1007/BF02101296 |s2cid=119128058}}</ref> and elliptic [[Macdonald polynomials]]).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Felder |first1=Giovanni |last2=Varchenko |first2=Alexander |author-link2=Alexander Varchenko |year=2004 |title=Hypergeometric theta functions and elliptic Macdonald polynomials |journal=International Mathematics Research Notices |volume=2004 |issue=21 |page=1037 |arxiv=math/0309452 |doi=10.1155/S1073792804132893 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

With [[Alberto Cattaneo]] in 2000 he gave a [[path integral formulation|path integral]] interpretation of [[Maxim Kontsevich|Kontsevich]]'s [[Kontsevich quantization formula|deformation quantization of Poisson manifolds]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cattaneo |first1=Alberto |author-link=Alberto Cattaneo |last2=Felder |first2=Giovanni |year=2000 |title=A Path Integral Approach to the Kontsevich Quantization Formula |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=212 |issue=3 |pages=591–611 |arxiv=math/9902090 |bibcode=2000CMaPh.212..591C |doi=10.1007/s002200000229 |s2cid=8510811}}</ref> as well as a description of the [[symplectic groupoid]] integrating a [[Poisson manifold]] as an infinite-dimensional [[symplectic quotient]].<ref>{{Citation |last1=Cattaneo |first1=Alberto |chapter=Poisson sigma models and symplectic groupoids |date=2001 |chapter-url=https://www.zora.uzh.ch/id/eprint/22010/9/ZORA22010V.pdf |title=Quantization of Singular Symplectic Quotients |pages=61–93 |place=Basel |publisher=Birkhäuser Basel |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-8364-1_4 |isbn=978-3-0348-9535-4 |access-date=2022-06-18 |last2=Felder |first2=Giovanni |s2cid=10248666 |author-link=Alberto Cattaneo|arxiv=math/0003023 |chapter-url-access= |url-status= |archive-url= |archive-date= }}</ref>

He supervised 22 doctoral students as of 2022, including [[Thomas Willwacher]].<ref name=":0" />
